metadata.title: [Kernel][SM70] Chunk block-scaled QPN8 decode through the M<=8 route for M=9..32
metadata.body:
# [Kernel][SM70] Chunk block-scaled QPN8 decode through the M<=8 route for M=9..32

## TL;DR

On SM70, block-scaled FP8 checkpoints (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, `weight_block_size [128,128]`) currently pay a **full dense-weight reconstruction before every GEMM on every decode step** with M=9..32 — i.e. every DFlash2/q8 speculative-decode step with ≥2 concurrent requests. Routing those steps through the already-accepted M≤8 direct-read kernels (8-row chunks) removes a **+45 ms/step** cliff: c=2 request wall **−48%**, the `fp8_qpn8_dequantize_sm70_kernel` goes **34 ms → 0 µs**, and per-row outputs are **bitwise identical** to single-stream decode.

## Symptom

DGX-1, 4×V100-SXM2 32GB TP4, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + DFlash2 q7 (uniform decode `query_len=8`), `max_num_seqs=4`: aggregate decode throughput at 2 concurrent requests was **below single-stream** (161 tok/s vs 200 tok/s at c=1) — negative scaling. Single-stream is unaffected (M=8), which hides the regression from any 1-user benchmark.

## Root cause (instrumented end-to-end)

Scale-format provenance for this checkpoint class:

1. Checkpoint stores `weight_scale_inv` as `[N/128, K/128]` (`weight_block_size [128,128]`; verified: `in_proj_qkv.weight_scale_inv` = `[80, 40]`).
2. At load, `fp8_qpn8_prepare_sm70` packs runtime `group_scales` to `[K/128, N/32]` fp16 (block layout).
3. In `fp8_qpn8_dispatch_sm70_out`, the M=9..32 direct-read candidates require the **channel** format (`group_scales == [1, N]`). Block layout → `channel_scales=false` → the candidates (including the existing M16/M32 chunked candidate, which is also channel-gated) never admit.
4. Fallback = `fp8_qpn8_prefill_sm70_out`: dequantize the **entire** weight, then FP16 cuBLAS. Sensible for prefill (amortized over hundreds of tokens), pathological for decode where it re-runs per GEMM per step.

Evidence chain:

- **Dispatch layer excluded**: instrumented `CudaGraphManager.dispatch` — 8/16/32-token uniform-decode steps all hit exact-size FULL graphs; no padding aliasing, no piecewise fallback. CPU schedule/sample < 0.4 ms/step.
- **Step profiling** (`target_forward` per engine step): M=8 → 20 ms; M=16 → **65 ms**; M=32 → 70-82 ms.
- **Kineto kernel delta** (M=16 step vs M=8 step): `fp8_qpn8_dequantize_sm70_kernel` +34 ms (absent at M=8), `volta_s884gemm_fp16` +16 ms, cutlass wmma +7 ms. (Kernel sum +57 ms vs step delta +45 ms: the kernel numbers come from differently-normalized trace windows; the step-level numbers are the authoritative ones.)
- **Interventional confirmation**: with this patch, decode-step dequantize time is **0 µs** and the cliff moves with it (below) — the fix doubles as the falsification test for the causal chain.

## The fix (~40 lines)

In `fp8_qpn8_dispatch_sm70_out`, for block-scaled weights at M=9..32, chunk through the accepted M≤8 route in 8-row slices (`input.narrow`/`out.narrow`, no allocation):

- `hc_dispatch_sm70_out` and `dispatch_ba_split_sm70_out` delegate to `dispatch_sm70_out` at m>8, so they inherit the fix.
- Env-gated default-on (`VLLM_SM70_FP8_QPN8_BLOCKSCALED_CHUNKED=0` restores the dequant fallback), with a log-once line when the route engages (previously the pathological path was completely silent).
- CUDA-graph-safe: the chunk loop only launches kernels on narrowed views of the caller's persistent buffers; validated inside FULL graphs at M=16/24/32 and inside PIECEWISE graphs at 256-1024 tokens.

## Numerics

Structural argument: the M≤8 kernels read `input` as fp16 directly (**no activation quantization**), `split_k`/`accumulator_chains` are per-layer constants fixed at weight-prepare time (M-independent), split-K partials reduce deterministically in shared memory (zero `atomicAdd` in the file), and `out` is write-only. Each output row is an independent dot product.

Verified empirically (standalone harness via `VLLM_QPN8_STANDALONE`, random 1024×512 weights, N=1024/K=512, split_k=4):

- **Batch-invariance, bitwise**: the same 8 input rows produce bitwise-identical outputs whether run standalone at M=8 or embedded at any position of an M=9/12/16/20/24/32 chunked batch (first and second chunk positions tested). Batching no longer changes per-row results — previously M=16 went through a different algorithm (dequant + cuBLAS) than M=8.
- **Distance to fp32 reference**: chunked route max-abs error 1.3-2.1e-5 vs 1.4-2.0e-5 for the old dequant route — same order; at M=9..16 the chunked route is slightly **closer** to fp32 than the old path. Old-vs-new outputs differ by ≤ 3.1e-5 (1-2 fp16 ulp at this magnitude), as expected for two different accumulation orders.
- End-to-end sentinel: DFlash2 accept-length statistics identical before/after (0.799 at c=1/2, 0.824 at c=4 over 5-round benches).

## Bench

384-token code fixture, streaming, min-wall of 5 rounds, same env/probes on both boots:

| concurrency | before | after | Δ | agg (req/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (M=8, path untouched) | 1.758 s | 1.839 s | see note | 0.66 |
| 2 (M=16) | 5.081 s | **2.631 s** | **−48%** | 0.44 → 0.70 |
| 4 (M=32) | 5.539 s | **4.182 s** | **−25%** | 0.76 → 0.94 |

Note (c=1): the M=8 path is untouched by this change; c=1 wall ranged 1.758-1.839 s across four boots with identical code paths (instrumentation env differs) — we read this as boot-to-boot noise, not regression; within-boot spread is tight (min 1.839 / median 1.847).

Note (c=4 exceeds the M=32 cost-model estimate): decode steps during the c=4 bench are not all M=32 — instrumented dispatch shows a mix of 8/16/24/32-token steps (requests finish staggered), and the M=16/24 steps gain 40-58%:

| step size | target_forward before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 8 tokens | ~20 ms | 20.7 ms (unchanged) |
| 16 tokens | 65 ms | **27.1 ms** (−58%) |
| 32 tokens | 70-82 ms | **40.0 ms** (−50%) |

## Known limits / follow-ups

- The chunked route re-reads the packed weight per 8-row chunk (M=16 ≈ 2×, M=32 ≈ 4× the M=8 GEMM time); M=32 lands near breakeven vs dequant at the kernel level (40 vs ~50 ms) and still wins e2e via the M≤24 mix. The durable fix is **native block-scale M16/M32 kernels** reading `[K/128, N/32]` scales directly (the M32 native scaffolding gated by `VLLM_SM70_FP8_QPN8_M32_NATIVE` is channel-only today) — happy to collaborate there.
- M > 32 still routes to the dequant fallback (unchanged).
- Prefill-path callers of `fp8_qpn8_prefill_sm70_out` are untouched.
- Validated stacked with the piecewise capture-ladder change (separate PR): both active together in the "after" numbers above.

## Repro

Any SM70 box, block-scaled FP8 Qwen3.8 + DFlash2 q7 (or any spec-decode config multiplying decode M past 8), 2 concurrent requests: aggregate decode drops below single-stream. Watch for `fp8_qpn8_dequantize_sm70_kernel` in a decode-step trace; with this patch it is absent and the log-once line fires.

## Related: mixed prefill+decode batches still run fully eager above 32 tokens (stacked-validation context)

The "after" numbers in this PR were measured with a wider piecewise capture ladder also active (stacked), so for completeness:

- Mixed steps (>32 tokens) currently find **no graph at all** — FULL decode graphs need uniform token counts, and default SM70 capture sizes stop at 32 vs `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`. The author has separately flagged mixed-batch eager as a concurrency item to fix.
- A/B with `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8,16,24,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192]}'` (same lane, this PR's sidecar also active):
  - dispatch instrumentation: all >32-token steps **NONE → 100% PIECEWISE** (184→256, 386→512, 563→1024 rungs)
  - mixed-step tail 280 → **185 ms**; mean ~65-66 ms (unchanged)
  - capture 25 s / 0.40 → 2.54 GiB; **GPU KV pool unchanged** (784,793 tokens); boot to healthy ~330 → ~336 s
  - e2e bench c=1/2/4: −1.5..3% (within cross-boot noise — mixed steps are ~2% of engine time on this deployment's traffic, so this is a tail-latency fix, not throughput)
- Proposal (kept out of this PR's scope): document the `cudagraph_capture_sizes` escape hatch; a **memory-aware** wider default (powers of two up to `min(max_num_batched_tokens, VRAM budget after KV sizing)`, graceful abort on the first rung that doesn't fit) would be the follow-up — a blanket wider default is unsafe on 16 GB V100s.

VL/multimodal steps not exercised in that A/B.

Reviewed against current main c98a8d664 as part of the maintainer-authorized 54633 acceptance pass. The chunking idea is useful, but the patch needs updating for the current per-engine native policy before it can merge. I am preparing the integration fix and will run the block-scale dense/gated and CUDA Graph cases on the V100 host.

[P1] The new branch calls env_enabled(), but current main has replaced the local env_enabled lambda with PolicyField/policy_exact_one. A three-way merge leaves this added call without a definition, so the resulting main does not compile. Please move this toggle into the existing per-engine native policy, preserving an explicit rollback setting, and cover M=9..32 block-scale dense/gated graph replay.
